name: Potato and Corn Empanadas With Aji

ingredients.name: jalapeño peppers, seeded and finely chopped
russet potato, peeled and cut into rough 1/4-inch cubes
loosely packed cilantro leaves, tender stems

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205°C (400°F). Heat oil in a large stainless steel skillet over medium high heat until shimmering. Add onion and garlic and cook, stirring, until soft, about 4 minutes. Add 1 jalapeño, potato, corn, and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a simmer and cover with a lid. Cook, stirring often until potatoes are just soft, about 8 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper and allow to cool.

Roll one recipe of pie dough out to 0.5 cm thickness and cut into six 10-cm rounds using a pastry cutter. Place 1/12th of filling on each round, brush edges with egg and using your fingers press to seal. Repeat with remaining filling and dough, then place on a lined baking sheet and bake until golden brown, about 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine remaining jalapeños, green onions, red onion, lime juice, and cilantro in a food processor and pulse until ingredients are very finely chopped. Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve with empanadas.

schema_metadata.keywords: aji, corn, empanadas, potatoes, Sunday Brunch

description: A bit spicy, a bit sweet, and a bit crunchy—these empanadas make a great light brunch, and even a great brown bag lunch if you have any left.
author: Sydney Oland
